newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta tourism down in September.
newsitem.headline: Malta tourism down in September.

text.p: Tourist arrivals for September dropped 5,750, or 4.7 percent, to 115,557, figures released on Tuesday by the Central Office of Statistics show.
The comparable arrivals figure for September 1995 was 121,307.

The British market, Malta's largest by far, saw a sharp decline of 8,758, or 16.2 percent, to 45,305 from 54,063 in September last year. There were also fewer French tourists, down 1,411 to 5,727, and fewer Belgians and other nationalities.
But more tourists came from, among other places, Germany, up by 1,300, Libya, up by 1,206, and the Netherlands, up by 1,087.

The overall drop for the first nine months this year was 55,386, or 6.1 percent, amounting to 846,293 visitors to Malta up to September this year, compared with 901,679 in the comparable period last year.

Tourism income in the first nine months was Lm171.4 ($480m) million, compared with Lm179.9 million in the same period last year. On a per capita basis, tourism earnings in the first nine months amounted to Lm202.5 this year from Lm199.5 in 1995.
